newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NZ SPORT-All Black reign coming to end-commentator.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-All Black reign coming to end-commentator.

text.p: SYDNEY, Aug 18 - The Dunedin Bledisloe Cup test signalled the beginning of the end for the present All Black dominance, according to an Australian rugby columnist who believes the Wallabies will win the 1999 World Cup.
Writing in today's Australian newspaper, Ewan Whitton says the All Blacks "looked surprisingly like a leaderless rabble" in the second half at Carisbrook.
"But this may seem only the inevitable conclusion of a sudden and sad descention in recent matches.
"The Springboks had them cold; the Australians outplayed them in the second half at Lancaster Park and were merely the worse of two bad teams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground."

The soft centre in the New Zealand pack became "really obvious" against South Africa a week ago and was then brilliantly exploited by Wallaby halfback David Knox early in the second half on Saturday, Whitton wrote.
The signs are there that several of the All Blacks have now become too old and their reactions too slow, he added.

Describing the first of two tries to Wallaby fullback Steve Larkham, Whitton wrote All Black prop Craig Dowd and Robin Brooke had him and lost him; flanker Josh Kronfeld and fullback Christian Cullen were slow to react; captain/hooker Sean Fitzpatrick and No 8 Zinzan Brooke didn't react at all.
He also criticises Frank Bunce, whom he said with two minutes of the match remaining was left staring "like a rabbit in the headlights" as Knox again drifted across field.
Under new management, and with ACT Brumbies prop Patricio Noriega cleared to play for Australia by 1999, Whitton said he would be inclined to back the Wallabies for the World Cup.
However, in the same newspaper Fitzpatrick is quoted saying the Wallabies would be fooling themselves if they considered their second-half comeback any form of moral victory.
Admitting he had expected more of Australia this season, Fitzpatrick said the All Blacks had found it unusual his former longstanding rival Phil Kearns had not been included in the Wallabies.
Kearns' form has not been considered good enough since a comeback from injury, but the New Zealand captain described him as a "special player", respected by New Zealanders.
New Zealand-born Sydney Morning Herald columnist Spiro Zavos contrasted Whitton's views, describing the Wallabies' fightback as "a case of Custer's last stand".
"Former Wallaby coach Bob Dwyer used to say he had no time for teams that opened up the game when it was already lost.
"Using Dwyer's argument, the Wallabies are not a good team," he wrote.
